## Purpose
FastAPI router (`/api/agents`) exposing agent-catalog reads (per-pipeline agent lists, the full agent library) and per-user CRUD for custom skills and prompt overrides, all scoped strictly to the calling user.

## Shape
- `AgentResponse` / `PipelineResponse` / `SkillRequest` / `SkillResponse` / `PromptOverrideRequest` / `AgentPromptResponse` — the Pydantic request/response models.
- `GET /pipelines/{pipeline_type}` and `GET /library` — read agent metadata from `agents.registry` (`get_pipeline_agents`, `get_all_agents_flat`, `get_agent_by_id`), annotating each with a `has_skill` hint via `_agent_has_resolvable_skill`.
- `GET/POST/DELETE /skills[/{agent_id}]` — per-user custom skill storage backed by `app.agents.skills` (`list_user_skills`, `read_user_skill`, `save_custom_skill`, `delete_custom_skill`), with a byte-size cap (`MAX_SKILL_BYTES`) enforced both by Pydantic `max_length` and an explicit UTF-8 byte check.
- `GET/PUT/DELETE /{agent_id}/prompt` — per-user prompt-override storage backed by `app.agents.prompt_overrides`, layered over the immutable base `AGENT.md` prompt body.
- Every endpoint depends on `get_current_user` and only touches that user's own files.

## Why this shape
The module docstring calls out a specific security constraint (Phase B G1-C7): user-controllable skill content is a prompt-injection vector, so it's capped at save time here and further sanitized/truncated at load time by the orchestrator — the double byte-check (Pydantic `max_length` plus an explicit UTF-8 length check) exists because Pydantic counts code points, not bytes, so multi-byte content needs the stricter explicit check to actually enforce the byte ceiling.
